Every once in a while I like to do a bit of distro hopping to see if I can find anything I prefer over Arch. The problem I have now is that I've gotten completely used to the rolling release model and I really don't want to go back, but there aren't that many rolling release distros around.

Does anyone have recommendations for RR distros that generally work pretty well?
Looking to do some distro hopping

You could try out PCLinuxOS but some packages and the kernel are fixed I think. It's rock solid though. RPM package management and choice of most popular DE's.

There's a version of OpenSuse as well that's a rolling release but I cant remember the name. A search should find it.
Gentoo, if you havent already considered it, but its a huge step up having to compile everything from source with emerge.
I'm really digging Devuan right now.... I'm currently running MATE on it.
Oh, and my RR suggestion is Linux Mint Debian Edition (MATE version).
I'm settling in to openSUSE Leap. Despite my bias, it seems to be a pretty solid distro. If you need rolling release, give Tumbleweed a go.

If you want rolling and you want to try something different then why not Gentoo? It may be a bit of a process to install, but afterwards its really not that bad to use and maintain. You get the benefit of a stable yet rolling distro that has very fine grained control, it truly lets you do whatever you want with it. For someone with a fair amount of Linux experience wanting to try something new I'd recommend it

Bonus is you can take your time installing it since you can do it from a chroot in an existing distribution installation

Void is rolling release. The core roles less frequently but the user packages seem are pretty close to Arch. I think they beat Arch on the Node update because that's where I first say 6 came out. They also keep a lot of the things you would only find in the AUR in the main repo like cdm (cli DM).

They have their own very simple init system.
